title: Intrinsic properness of representable algebraic-space maps is tested on schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Properness for algebraic-space morphisms has its intrinsic meaning [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]: separated, quasi-compact, locally of finite type on compatible etale scheme charts, and universally closed after every algebraic-space base change. Assume $f$ is representable by schemes: for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every map $h_T\to Y$, the sheaf fibre product $X\times_Yh_T$ is represented by an $S$-scheme $X_T$. Write $f_T:X_T\to T$ for its projection. Then $f$ is proper if and only if $f_T$ is a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism] for every such $T\to Y$. The equivalence does not require finite presentation, Noetherian hypotheses, flatness, or quasi-compactness in advance.

source.place: Tag 083R (lemma-proper-local), equivalence (1) and (2), specialized to representable morphisms, with the agreement for represented scheme maps in Section Tag 03HA (section-representable).

proof.text: Assume $f$ is intrinsically proper and fix any scheme $T\to Y$. In [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] quasi-compactness of $f$ asks that every pullback of $f$ to an affine scheme has quasi-compact point space; by the last clause of [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] this holds exactly when that pullback admits a surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme, which is the quasi-compactness of [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change]. So $f$ is proper in the sense of that lemma, and by [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change] the algebraic-space projection $X\times_Yh_T\to h_T$ is intrinsically proper. Representability identifies it with the map $h_{X_T}\to h_T$. Its separatedness says that the scheme diagonal of $f_T$ is a closed immersion: use the identity scheme test of that diagonal. Its local finite type agrees with scheme local finite type by [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test]. Its quasi-compactness gives scheme quasi-compactness by [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests], taking the identity test over $T$. Its universal closedness, restricted to scheme base changes, gives scheme universal closedness. Here the point topology on a represented scheme is its usual topology: the identity scheme atlas is a quotient presentation in [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. These four conditions are precisely scheme properness [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus every $f_T$ is proper.

Conversely assume every $f_T$ is proper. Scheme properness [def-weil-proper-morphism] includes finite type, hence quasi-compactness. The representable-morphism clause of [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests] therefore makes $f$ quasi-compact. By its equivalent clause on affine schemes, for every affine scheme $V\to Y$ the space $X\times_YV$ admits a surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme, so its point space is quasi-compact by the last clause of [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]; this is quasi-compactness of $f$ in [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. This uses all scheme tests, without requiring the schemes $T$ or $Y$ to be quasi-compact.

Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to Y$, which exists by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The pullback $X_V=X\times_YV$ is a scheme by the hypothesis on $f$; the fibre product exists by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Its map $f_V:X_V\to V$ is proper and therefore locally of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] to the target atlas $V\to Y$ and the identity source atlas $X_V\to X_V$. Its locally-of-finite-type clause gives that $f$ is locally of finite type. Together with step 2 this is finite type in [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties].

source.place: Tag 040Y (lemma-finite-type-local), compatible atlas criterion, used by 083R.

proof.text: To prove separatedness, put $D=X\times_YX$. Its diagonal is representable by [lem-sfb-space-diagonal-scheme-tests]. Fix a scheme test $T\to D$, with components $a,b:T\to X$ and common composite $t:T\to Y$. The maps $a,b$ define sections $\widetilde a,\widetilde b:T\to X_T$ of $f_T$. The universal property of the sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] identifies $X\times_DT\to T$ with the pullback of $\Delta_{f_T}:X_T\to X_T\times_TX_T$ along $(\widetilde a,\widetilde b)$: on any test scheme both classify equality of the two sections. Since $f_T$ is proper, $\Delta_{f_T}$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Its pullback is a closed immersion by clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Every scheme test of $\Delta_f$ is thus a closed immersion, so $f$ is separated by [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties].

source.place: Tag 03KM (lemma-separated-local), diagonal scheme-test argument in its proof; scheme base change of closed immersions is Tag 01QR.

proof.text: It remains to prove universal closedness. Fix any algebraic-space map $Z\to Y$ and put $p:E=X\times_YZ\to Z$ using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $q:W\to Z$ as in [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. Then $E_W=E\times_ZW=X\times_YW$ is the scheme $X_W$, and $p_W:E_W\to W$ is proper by the hypothesis on all scheme tests. Let $C\subseteq|E|$ be closed. The projection $r:E_W\to E$ has scheme source, so it is continuous by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. Thus $C_W=r^{-1}(C)$ is closed. The point topology on $E_W$ is the scheme topology, since its identity atlas supplies the quotient presentation. As $p_W$ is scheme proper, $p_W(C_W)$ is closed by universal closedness in [def-weil-proper-morphism], applied to the identity base change.

source.place: Tag 03XD (lemma-characterize-representable-universally-closed), scheme atlas of the arbitrary base change; Tag 03IT (lemma-universally-closed-local).

proof.text: We have $q^{-1}(p(C))=p_W(C_W)$. The inclusion from right to left follows from $pr=qp_W$. For the other, choose $w\in|W|$ with $q(w)=p(e)$ for some $e\in C$, and a field representative $c:\operatorname{Spec}K\to E$ of $e$. Apply [lem-a1-space-fibre-product-point] with algebraic-space target $Z$ and scheme sources $\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $W$. It supplies a point over $w$ and the chosen representative, whose image in $E\times_ZW$ lies in $C_W$ and maps to $w$. Thus the asserted equality holds. Since $q$ is a quotient map by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover], closedness of $p_W(C_W)$ implies closedness of $p(C)$. The subset $C$ and the algebraic-space base change $Z\to Y$ were arbitrary, so $f$ is universally closed [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties].

source.place: Tag 03XD (lemma-characterize-representable-universally-closed), image equality and quotient-topology inference; point lifting is spaces-properties.tex Tag 03H4.

proof.text: Steps 2 and 3 give finite type, step 4 gives separatedness, and steps 5 and 6 give universal closedness. By [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], $f$ is proper. Together with step 1 this proves the equivalence. No step used finite presentation, Noetherianity, flatness, or an advance quasi-compactness assumption.
